q: Halogens are diatomic molecules and include fluorine, chlorine, bromine, and iodine.
e: Halogens exist as diatomic molecules in their elemental form.

q: Fluorine is a solid at room temperature.
e: Fluorine is a gas at room temperature.

q: Chlorine is a pale green gas with a choking smell.
e: Chlorine has a distinct pale green color and a strong odor.

q: Bromine is a solid at room temperature.
e: Bromine is a liquid at room temperature.

q: Iodine is a purple-black shiny solid that sublimes when heated.
e: Iodine sublimes to form violet vapor when heated.

q: Halogens can be found in nature in their elemental forms.
e: Halogens are not found in nature as elemental forms; they exist as salts.

q: Chlorine is less reactive than fluorine.
e: Fluorine is the most reactive halogen, more so than chlorine.

q: Halogens react with hydrogen to form hydrogen halides.
e: Halogens readily react with hydrogen to form hydrogen halides.

q: Iodine is more reactive than bromine.
e: Bromine is more reactive than iodine.

q: Chlorine can displace bromine from sodium bromide solution.
e: Chlorine is more reactive and can displace bromine from its compounds.

q: Bromine is a stronger oxidizing agent than chlorine.
e: Chlorine is a stronger oxidizing agent than bromine.

q: Halogens react with alkalis to form halides.
e: Halogens react with alkalis to produce halides.

q: The presence of halide ions can be tested using silver nitrate solution.
e: Silver nitrate solution is used to test for halide ions.

q: Chlorine does not have bleaching properties.
Bromine reacts with metals to form metal bromides.
e: Bromine reacts with metals to form corresponding bromides.

q: The reactivity of halogens decreases from fluorine to iodine.
e: The reactivity of halogens decreases in the order of F, Cl, Br, I.

q: Halides are positively charged ions formed from halogens.
e: Halides are negatively charged ions formed from halogens.

q: Iodine can displace chlorine from sodium chloride solution.
e: Iodine cannot displace chlorine from sodium chloride solution.

q: Chlorine reacts with water to form hydrochloric acid and hypochlorous acid.
e: Chlorine reacts with water to produce HCl and HOCl.
